name: Kansas
agency: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, with a licensed adult 21+ (25 before a restricted license at 15; affidavit of the full 50 before 16). Driver education behind-the-wheel time counts if the instructor is 21+; observation time does not (KDOR teen FAQ).
teen.holdPermit: 1 year before a restricted license (DE-99 driver-ed permit time does not count); under 17, 1 year or until 17, whichever comes first, before the driving test (handbook p. 12, 94)
teen.nightLimit: Restricted license at 16 (first 6 months): may drive 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., plus work, school and school activities, religious activities, or any time with a licensed adult in the front seat. At 15: only work, home-school by the most direct route on school days, religious activities (6 a.m. to 9 p.m. per K.S.A. 8-2,101), or any time with a licensed adult beside the driver (handbook p. 12-13).
teen.passengerLimit: Under 16: no non-sibling minor passengers. At 16, first six months: no more than one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family (handbook p. 12-13; K.S.A. 8-2,101(d)).
teen.phone: Permit and restricted license holders: no wireless communication device while driving except to report illegal activity or summon emergency help (handbook p. 12-13). All drivers: no writing, sending or reading texts/email while driving (K.S.A. 8-15,111; handbook p. 19 cites 8-1598).

bac.under21: 0.02 (handbook p. 23; K.S.A. 8-1567a: first occurrence .02-.08 is a 30-day suspension, second 1 year)

notes: Handbook: Kansas Driving Handbook, Non-Commercial Driver's Manual, AAMVA 09 Model Test Version, 'Revised February 2022' (PDF built 2023-02-21), read 2026-10-09. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers.
Spanish handbook (dlhb-sp.pdf) exists but is an older edition (Rev. Feb 2019).

Knowledge test: 25 multiple-choice questions, 80% to pass (20 of 25), untimed; 4 attempts, then wait 6 months (handbook p. 13-14, 94). May be taken at a full-service office or online at ks.knowtodrive.com.
Test languages: the official KDOR online test (KnowToDrive, linked from the handbook) offers English and Spanish with audio. The handbook does not list languages for the in-office test.
Permit: licensed adult at least 21 with one year of driving experience in the front seat; no one else in the front seat (handbook p. 12).

Restricted license at 15 requires an approved driver education course (not internet courses). If the 50-hour affidavit is not provided, restrictions continue until 17 (KDOR teen FAQ; K.S.A. 8-2,101(h)).
Speed (handbook p. 62): 75 mph on separated multilane highways where designated and posted; 65 on state or federal highways; 55 on county or township highways.
Stop for a stopped school bus, church bus or day care bus loading children; opposing traffic on a divided highway need not stop (handbook p. 18; K.S.A. 8-1556).
Seat belts: illegal to drive or ride in front without one (handbook p. 27); primary enforcement since June 2010 (KHP).

Move over: 2025 SB 8 (signed; effective on statute-book publication, July 1, 2025) extends move-over to any stopped, standing or parked vehicle showing hazard lamps, flares or caution signals: change lanes away if possible and safe, otherwise slow down. Enrolled bill read on kslegislature.org. The 2022 handbook (p. 18, 85) covers only emergency and tow vehicles.
